title: Are the 'verdict heads' a moral judgment circuit or a digit-answer circuit?
why: verdict-trace found where the 0-4 wrongness DIGIT is written (reply onset, L19-23) and five heads that write it (L23 H0, L21 H19, L23 H26, L22 H5, L23 H25; L23 H1 opposes). verdict-transfer then showed the onset diff-of-means direction is digit geometry: on a reversed acceptability scale it raises the digit, and it does nothing to yes/no or free text. So the map may be of the digit answer, not the judgment. This run repeats the map and the surgery in formats whose answer token is NOT a wrongness digit, and patches states ACROSS formats.
model: Qwen/Qwen3-4B, forward passes only, score level.

formats.J: kestrel wrongness prompt (0-4, 4 = extremely wrong). Wrongness metric W = logsumexp(lp 3,4) - logsumexp(lp 0,1,2).
formats.REV: acceptability 0-4 (0 = completely unacceptable). Wrongness metric W = -(logsumexp(lp 3,4) - logsumexp(lp 0,1,2)), so that higher = more wrong in every format.
formats.YN: 'Is the behavior described morally acceptable? Answer with Yes or No.' W = lp(No) - lp(Yes).

items: Social Norms (16) as recipients; top tercile by J (38) as donors; bottom tercile (38) as second recipient set for the ablation readout.

parts.P1_map: Per format: donor (top) -> recipient (social) residual patch at the onset, layers 14-30, 48 pairs (3 donors each). T = (W_patched - W_r) / (W_d - W_r).
parts.P2_cross: Cross-format patch at layers 18-26: donor state from format X (top item) into recipient format Y (social item), for (X, Y) in {(J, YN), (YN, J), (YN, REV), (J, REV)}. T_cross = (W_patched - W_r) / (mean W_top(Y) - mean W_social(Y)): the fraction of format Y's own gap that a foreign-format donor state transfers.
parts.P3_ablate: Mean-ablate V5 and R4 (verdict-trace) and 40 random 5-sets and 40 random 4-sets from layers {18, 20, 21, 22, 23} (seed 21), all positions, separately under REV and YN. Readout per format: wrongness contrast gap = mean W(top) - mean W(social).
parts.P4_heads: Single-head onset patches of the V5 heads and L23 H1, donor (top) -> recipient (social) within REV and within YN, 48 pairs each.

hypotheses.C1_yes_no_band: In YN, P1 onset transfer is < 0.1 at L18 and > 0.5 by L26: the yes/no verdict is written in the same band as the digit.
hypotheses.C2_format_independent_state: P2: T_cross >= 0.5 at some layer in 20-26 for BOTH (J -> YN) and (YN -> J). If both stay < 0.2, the onset states are format-specific answer states, not a shared judgment.
hypotheses.C3_heads_carry_judgment: P3: V5 ablation shrinks the YN wrongness gap below >= 95% of the 40 random 5-sets (rank p <= 0.05), AND does the same for the REV gap.
hypotheses.C4_same_heads_write_it: P4: the summed single-head transfer of the V5 heads in YN is >= 50% of their summed transfer in J (verdict-trace CONFIRM sum 0.711), AND the same in REV.

readings: C2 + C3 + C4 -> the verdict heads carry a format-general moral judgment; the digit-geometry problem was specific to the diff-of-means direction. C3/C4 fail -> verdict-trace mapped a digit-answer circuit; the format-general judgment lives elsewhere (or nowhere linear). C1 alone -> each format writes its answer in the same band, which is where answers get written, not necessarily judgments.
notes: run.py imports ../verdict-trace-tanager/common.py. Rows -> rows.jsonl. XF_SMOKE=1 -> discarded.
